tecnicas.observacao: Prompt em três etapas: análise da tarefa (raciocinio), planejamento dos passos de codificação com quebra em subproblemas (decomposicao) e pedido explícito de código Python 3 em formato Markdown (instrucao, restricoes). O caso de uso do Fibonacci (p. 3-4, Fig. 2) descreve geração de várias hipóteses por nó, avaliação e escolha do melhor ramo, mas o prompt impresso só contém as três etapas e o artigo não descreve busca em árvore com várias chamadas ou seleção automática; por isso amostragem/feedback não foram atribuídos. O estudo não executa condição sem ToT (por exemplo, zero-shot); a comparação é com números publicados por Ouyang et al. [3], logo não há condição contrafactual.

citacoes.trecho: This paper showcases the Tree of Thoughts (ToT) prompting strategy as a promising alternative for improving the predictability and quality of code generation results.

Our experiments on GPT-3.5 Turbo model using 829 code generation problems from benchmarks such as CodeContests, APPS (Automated Programming Progress Standard) and HumanEval demonstrate a substantial reduction in non-determinism compared to previous findings.
This non-deterministic behavior can undermine the validity of scientific conclusions drawn from LLM-based experiments.
Non-deterministically generated code may contain errors, inconsistencies, or inefficiencies, limiting its practical utility [6].

Unlike the standard methods of evaluating code generation by LLMs [20], where a simple zero-shot prompt is used, our ToT approach involves creating structured prompts in multiple steps to guide the LLM in generating correct and deterministic code.
Step 2: Plan the coding steps in Python (breaking down the problem into sub-problems).
Step 3: Generate Python 3 code in Markdown format.
To enable ChatGPT to produce five distinct predictions from the same prompt, we perform five successive API calls.

To ensure that test cases are executed sequentially and to prevent concurrency issues that could arise from simultaneous executions, we use scripts called monothread (instructions are executed in the order they are written).
The original test set contains 5,000 problems, and we randomly sample 500 problems.
In our study, we examine the influence of temperature in RQ3 with three temperature values: 0, 1, and 2.

These results show a drastic reduction in semantic variability for the CodeContests and APPS datasets compared to the results of Ouyang and al. [3] which show percentages of 72.73%; 60.40% for the same datasets.

For HumanEval, the reduction in semantic variability is less pronounced (from 65.85% to 69%), which may indicate that the tasks in this dataset present unique challenges that are not fully mitigated by TOT.
Due to the limited financial resources (300 $) available for this work, we only present the results for the APPS dataset, with which we were able to experiment with all temperature values.
A temperature of 0 promotes accuracy, similarity, and determinism, while a temperature of 2 leads to excessive creativity that hinders the quality and similarity of the generated code.

citacoes.trecho: Table II shows percentages of coding tasks without a single identical test output among the five different requests of 4.32%; 9%; and 69% for the CodeContests, APPS, and HumanEval datasets, respectively.
Specifically, we observed a significant decrease in the number of coding tasks that produced inconsistent outputs across multiple requests.
